title: Web: operations and settings
summary: The operations and settings family is careful where it matters most and is well covered end to end. Secret fields are uncontrolled and cleared before sending, every success body goes through a generated runtime parser, settings writes carry expected_version, every control comes from components/ui/field.tsx (the harness check passes), and browser suites check refusals, stale writes and that no key leaks. The cost is in how each panel is built: each one hand-rolls its own view-state machine. Three panels write their initial read twice, because react-hooks/set-state-in-effect forbids calling load() from the effect. The save flow exists in five copies that have drifted. Failure bodies are cast instead of parsed with the generated parseErrorResponse, which apps/web never uses. Busy is cleared before the success body is parsed, so a parse error escapes as an unhandled rejection. There are three different conflict strategies, and the retention save reports one validation rule for every failure. Its days() parser turns "1,000" into 1 and "3O" into 3, ahead of a timed worker pass that deletes run content. Loading, unavailable and denied states look and announce differently, blur their causes and offer no retry. The measured leads hold: OperationsPanel (377 lines, complexity 28) and ModelPolicyPanel (350) need splitting, and ProviderSettingsPanel (222) less urgently. The small private subcomponents behind the no-multi-comp hits are fine. Pure formatting sits in client components with no fast tests. Operations keys its lookup tables by string although the contract has unions. role_overrides is cast over a runtime gap. Appearance preferences are defined both in the control and in the root layout's before-paint script.

scores.why: Strict TS, the shared field controls (harness check passes) and semantic tokens are followed. Arbitrary pixel type sizes, eight copied token literals, four untitled pages and unassociated help text fall short of DH-06 and DS-03.

Dependencies point the right way (generated client, small lib helpers). But each panel embeds its own read, send and state machinery, and the appearance preference table is split between the control and the root layout.
OperationsPanel (377 lines, complexity 28), ModelPolicyPanel (350) and ProviderSettingsPanel (222) each hold a whole screen. Three of the five component files exceed 300 lines.

Small pure helpers exist (perMillion, sameForm, sourceLabel, schemaValue). But the panels mix fetching, mutation, draft state, formatting and layout, and the provider mutate reports one outcome for every action.
Pages are thin Server Components under a settings layout. But feature components sit flat among 43 files, a page link lives inside a panel, and the settings section layout is copied page by page.
One consistent path (BFF, generated parsers, CSRF, expected_version), but implemented as a hand-written state machine per panel. The lint-forced duplicate read and client-only initial reads add cost.
Comments explain why and cite decisions and PRD IDs. A few are cryptic ('Its name holds the database's') or slightly wrong ('Numbers only' above values that include text).

Success bodies use the generated parsers, and two panels use exhaustive union-keyed maps. But four failure bodies and three role_overrides values are cast, operations keys its maps by string, and preferences are string-typed.

A misparse can silently shorten retention, and success-path parse errors escape as unhandled rejections. Failures are cast and sometimes misreported. Unavailable, denied and signed-out states blur together, with no retry.

Browser suites cover flows, refusals, stale versions and secret leakage well, but they need the db profile. The pure helpers in these panels have no fast tests, and the one precedent, schema-value.test.ts, runs in no verify profile (WSHL-08).
The code behaves carefully and is well tested end to end. But changing save or error behavior means editing five drifting copies, and the two largest panels need splitting first.

strengths.title: Secrets never enter React state or props
strengths.evidence: The OpenRouter key and tool secrets are read from an uncontrolled field through FormData, and the form is reset before the request (apps/web/components/provider-settings-panel.tsx:221-232, apps/web/components/keys-and-vars-panel.tsx:65-72). The fields use type=password, autoComplete=off and data-1p-ignore (provider-settings-panel.tsx:313-322), and a secret's value is never rendered (keys-and-vars-panel.tsx:88-95). Browser suites check that the field is cleared and that page content, responses and logs never contain the key (apps/web/tests/browser/settings.spec.ts:107,117,125,408; settings-keys-and-vars.spec.ts:161,184).

strengths.title: Generated runtime parsers on every success body, no-store reads
strengths.evidence: parseLocalStatus, parseModelList, parseModelPolicyState, parseProviderStatus and parseKeysAndVars validate each success body instead of casting it (operations-panel.tsx:176,194; model-policy-panel.tsx:147-148,175,202; provider-settings-panel.tsx:166,179,210; keys-and-vars-panel.tsx:173,186,217). Every read sends cache: "no-store".

strengths.title: Exhaustive label maps keyed by generated unions
strengths.evidence: provider-settings-panel.tsx:19-63 declares Record<ProviderStatus["auth_status"], string> and similar maps. keys-and-vars-panel.tsx:18-35 keys TITLES and USES by KeyOrVar["name"]. account/page.tsx:10 maps the role union. A new enum value then fails type checking. This is the model for operations-panel.

strengths.title: Shared form controls with explicit labels
strengths.evidence: Every input, select and radio comes from apps/web/components/ui/field.tsx (operations-panel.tsx:506,515; model-policy-panel.tsx:356,400; provider-settings-panel.tsx:313; keys-and-vars-panel.tsx:107,117; appearance-control.tsx:163,185,194,220,244). Each is labelled through htmlFor or a wrapping label. tests/harness/test_shared_form_controls.py was run during this review: 2 tests passed.

strengths.title: Optimistic concurrency and honest saved state
strengths.evidence: Every settings write sends expected_version (model-policy-panel.tsx:167,198; provider-settings-panel.tsx:230,358; keys-and-vars-panel.tsx:247,250) with a specific stale_version message (model-policy-panel.tsx:184-186,213-215). RoleEffect describes only the saved policy (72-116). A saved choice that is no longer offered stays visible and is flagged (232-252, 329-345), so the browser stays a view of durable state.

strengths.title: Comments that explain why, with traceable IDs
strengths.evidence: Examples: 'Cleared before the request, so the key never waits in the form, in any outcome.' (provider-settings-panel.tsx:226). 'Read, or an unread refusal holds its connection open...' (model-policy-panel.tsx:142). 'A refused save keeps what was typed' (operations-panel.tsx:223). The hydration note at appearance-control.tsx:141. The file header at keys-and-vars-panel.tsx:16-17 cites Decisions 0024 and 0025 and PK-04 to PK-08.

strengths.title: Thin server pages and a hydration-safe appearance control
strengths.evidence: Most pages are 11 to 28-line Server Components that put the client boundary at the interactive panel (apps/web/app/operations/page.tsx, settings/models/page.tsx, settings/keys-and-vars/page.tsx). settings/layout.tsx:5-6 records the tab-order reasoning. appearance-control.tsx:98-124 handles unreadable or unwritable storage, and 141-148 gates checked state on mount without suppressing warnings, as DS-02 asks.

strengths.title: Meaning carried by words, indicators decorative
strengths.evidence: Status dots and icons are aria-hidden and only repeat the text (operations-panel.tsx:79,91,242-256,310-316, with an sr-only separator at 309; provider-settings-panel.tsx:51,70-80). This follows DS-03: never infer state from color alone.

findings.title: Retention day fields misparse typos before a destructive retention pass

locations.note: days() keeps leading digits and maps any other text to null
save() sends the parsed values unchecked and reports Saved on any 2xx
free-text inputs: inputMode=numeric only, no validation or error association
the worker applies every declared window on a timer
the server accepts any whole number from 1 to 36500, so it cannot see the misparse

findings.impact: A 1,000-day window typed with a thousands separator is stored as one day. The worker's next timed pass (apply_all) then removes the checkpoints, working files and artifact bytes of every run that finished more than a day ago. The loss is irreversible and is reported as a success; the only hint is the refreshed field showing 1. A mistyped value can also silently clear a window.
findings.recommendation: Parse each field strictly in a pure helper: empty means keep everything, and otherwise only whole digits are accepted. Then validate the draft with the generated parseRetentionSettings, which already checks the contract's 1 to 36500 bounds, instead of copying the bounds. On a bad value, send nothing, set aria-invalid on that input and point aria-describedby at an inline message. Leave the cross-field rule to the server. Because the API hides validation details ('The request is not valid.'), show today's rule sentence only for code invalid_request, and show the server's message for other refusals. Cover the inputs above with node:test cases.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: validate data at trust boundaries and build accessible forms. The server's RetentionSettings validation stays the authority, including the cross-field rule. The client checks only format and reuses the generated range, so no retention rule moves into Next.js.
findings.verifierNote: Re-ran days() in node ('1,000' gives 1, '3O' 3, '2e3' 2, '7.9' 7, 'abc' null); apply_retention purges every finished run older than run_days on the worker's timed pass (retention.py:92-158, worker.py:217-219), and the contract accepts any whole number from 1 to 36500.

findings.title: Five save flows hand-roll request, parsing and messages, and they have drifted

locations.note: busy is cleared at 208, before the parse at 210; the failure body is cast at 213
the same mutate, differing only in path, parser and success text
save: cast at 179; stale_version asks for a page reload
resetAll: a near-copy of save
no catch around csrfFetch, no busy state, and one fixed rule sentence for any failure
Check again has no busy state either
the family's one try/catch/finally save, a local precedent
ErrorResponse and parseErrorResponse are generated; apps/web never uses them

findings.impact: Changing how a save reports failure, conflict or progress means five edits to copies that already disagree. The policy panel asks for a page reload on stale_version (184-186), while provider and keys refetch after any failure (217, 224). Retention shows a validation rule for a 401, 403 or 503 (218-221) and leaves a network failure unhandled. An error body that drifts from {code, message} is trusted through a cast and rendered.
findings.recommendation: Add one non-throwing sendJson helper, built once in apps/web/lib and shared with the web-shell forms (WSHL-06 proposes the same helper; agree one outcome shape). It wraps csrfFetch, parses 2xx bodies with the generated parser and refusals with parseErrorResponse, and returns a discriminated outcome. Add a small useMutation hook that owns busy (cleared in finally) and a typed notice, with per-call wording for success, stale_version and fallback. Panels then keep only path, body, parser and words. Give Save retention and Check again the same busy state. Keep the strings the browser suites pin (settings.spec.ts:83, 87, 142 and 219, models.spec.ts:189, settings-keys-and-vars.spec.ts:160 and 206, operations.spec.ts:51), or update them in the same change.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: centralize error handling, parse responses explicitly at untrusted boundaries, avoid blanket type assertions, and disable duplicate submits while expected_version stays the correctness mechanism. This consumes the generated parseErrorResponse; generated.ts is not edited.
findings.verifierNote: Flows, the busy-before-parse order and the casts confirmed (19 failure-body casts in 15 files, no parseErrorResponse use). Lowered to medium: success bodies are parsed, and the unhandled paths need a contract-violating 2xx or an unreachable Next server, as XDUP-07 and WSHL-06 rate the same pattern.

findings.title: Three panels write their initial read twice, because the effect may not call load()

locations.note: load and the mount effect; only load handles a null reply and clears failed
load and the mount effect
load and the mount effect
drains refused bodies, because 'an unread refusal holds its connection open'
refusals left unread here, as in provider 180-181 and keys 187-188
the one settings page that reads on the server and passes initial data
requestJson puts the HTTP status only inside its message

findings.evidence: I replaced keys-and-vars-panel's effect with useEffect(() => { void load(); }, [load]) and linted it from stdin, with no file written. It fails react-hooks/set-state-in-effect (eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7.1.1), so each panel inlines a second fetch-and-parse. The copies drift. load lets a parse error escape from void load() (operations 176 and 286) or await load() (provider 217, keys 224), while the effect's .catch turns the same error into the unavailable state. The policy panel drains refused bodies for a stated reason that the other three ignore. git grep for `const load = useCallback` finds 4 components that pair a load callback with an inline mount fetch: these 3 and approvals-panel.tsx.
findings.impact: Every change to how a panel reads (error codes, retry, draining refusals) has to be made twice per panel, and the two copies already react differently to the same failure.
findings.recommendation: Give each resource one module-level reader that never throws and returns a discriminated result (value, signed_out, denied, unavailable). Apply it from the effect's .then and from refresh. The same probe rewritten this way, with readKeysAndVars and an apply callback, lints clean (exit 0). Keep one shape across screens: tool-catalog.tsx:156-181 already has a typed useLoaded that WTAP-01 proposes promoting to lib with a reload, so extend it with these problem kinds rather than adding a third shape. Longer term, the Server Component pages could read initial data on the server with the generated getLocalStatus, getModelPolicy, getModelProviders, getKeysAndVars and getModels, as AccountPage reads its session, leaving the client panels for interaction. That first needs requestJson to expose the HTTP status as a field (WSHL-03) and service-status' module-private memberClient to be exported.
findings.ruleCheck: This keeps react-hooks/set-state-in-effect on rather than weakening lint. DH-06 prefers Server Components for the longer-term option. Reads stay per request and no-store, and by contract none of these bodies carries a secret.
findings.verifierNote: Both stdin lint probes reproduced (calling load() fails react-hooks/set-state-in-effect; the module-level reader exits 0). Count corrected from 5 to 4 components; memberClient is module-private, so the server-read option needs it exported.

locations.note: bare alert paragraph; loading has role=status
Card alert; 'Loading models.' has no role
Card alert; 'Loading settings.' has no role
Card alert; 'Loading settings.' has no role

fetchSession returns null both when signed out and on any failure

findings.evidence: Three panels show '<X> unavailable. Sign in, and check that the local API is running.' for any non-OK or network failure; only operations tells a 403 apart. Loading reads 'Loading…' with role=status in one panel, and 'Loading models.' or 'Loading settings.' without a role in the others. No failed state offers a retry, and operations' Check again button unmounts with the data when a refresh fails. /settings/models stacks two loading lines or two unavailable cards. Outcome notices (policy 463-472, provider 291-295, keys 262-266, operations 527-531) render success and refusal alike: role=status, plain text, no destructive tone or icon.
findings.impact: Users cannot tell signed out, denied and unreachable apart, and must reload the page to recover. A signed-in user whose API is down is told to sign in. Each new panel copies one of four variants.
findings.recommendation: Add components/ui/panel-state.tsx. It covers loading (role=status) and the signed_out, denied and unavailable problems (role=alert in a Card, with an icon and an optional Retry). Feed it from the shared reader's result, which maps the BFF codes. Make the outcome notice a {tone, text} pair, and render refusals with role=alert, the destructive tone and an icon. settings.spec.ts:83, 87 and 142 find provider refusals by role=status, so update them in the same change. On the account page, call fetchServiceStatus() beside fetchSession(), as the home page does (app/page.tsx:33-38).
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: represent loading, empty, denied, unavailable and retryable states deliberately. DS-03: errors use the destructive tone plus an explicit label or icon. Keep the hooks the browser tests pin (data-state=policy-unavailable and the 403 sentence).
findings.verifierNote: Variants, the unmounting Check again and the null-session Sign in confirmed. Added that settings.spec.ts:83, 87 and 142 read refusals by role=status and must move with the role change.

findings.title: role_overrides casts hide that its values are never checked at runtime

locations.note: as Record<string, string>
as Record<string, string>
profile cast to the ModelProfileId union
only additionalProperties === false is enforced; a schema-valued one is skipped
the schema says each value is a ModelProfileId
the generated type is Record<string, unknown>

findings.evidence:
```tsx
const saved = state.role_overrides as Record<string, string>;   // 55
setOverrides(next.role_overrides as Record<string, string>);   // 130
notOffered.has(profile as (typeof listed)[number]["profile"])  // 251
```
parseModelPolicyState passes role_overrides through checkObject. That function validates named properties and rejects extras only when additionalProperties is false, so the $ref to ModelProfileId on each value is never applied. The generator emits Record<string, unknown> for any object without properties (scripts/generate_contracts.py:46-47).
findings.impact: A drifted override (a renamed profile, or a number) is accepted by the parser and then trusted by three casts. The form would show it as a selected value with no matching option, and sameForm would compare it as a string.
findings.recommendation: Narrow once, in lib/model-policy.ts. roleOverrides(state) checks each key against the roles bound in state.policy.bindings and each value with the generated parseModelProfileId, and returns Partial<Record<ModelRole, ModelProfileId>>. An unknown role or profile throws ContractError, so the panel shows its unavailable state. It never drops or displays the value, because Save sends the whole map and would then delete the server's override. Use it in sameForm, adopt and the not-offered check. The root fix belongs to the api-client runtime and generator (WSHL-01): check schema-valued additionalProperties and emit typed records, then regenerate. Do not edit generated.ts.
findings.ruleCheck: contracts.md: generated TypeScript consumes the Pydantic/OpenAPI contract, and TypeScript types do not validate JSON. Ground rule: generated files are regenerated, never hand-edited. DH-06: no blanket type assertions.
findings.verifierNote: Casts at 55, 130 and 251, checkObject's skip (runtime.ts:71-78) and the generator rule confirmed. Recommendation revised: an unknown role or profile must fail like a contract error, since silently dropping it would make the next Save delete the server's override.

findings.evidence: Nine pure helpers are module-private in client components: valueFor, gb, days, perMillion, fetchedAt, sameForm, sourceLabel, and appearance's read and apply. apps/web/tests/unit holds three files, and only schema-value.test.ts covers this area; otherwise the helpers are checked only by Playwright suites in the db profile on a disposable stack. Formatting has already drifted. Plurals are hand-written twice and missing once ('1 hours ago.'). Counts use Intl in one branch and not the next. Dates appear as ISO strings here and as locale text in the policy panel.
findings.impact: A wording, rounding or parsing change needs the slowest profile to check, and defects such as days() and the hour plural go unseen until someone reads the screen.
findings.recommendation: Move the helpers into lib/ beside schema-value.ts (operations-format.ts, retention.ts, model-policy.ts, and appearance read/apply with injected storage), keep them free of '@/' aliases and other imports that node --test cannot resolve, export them, and add node:test files under apps/web/tests/unit. Register each new file in verify.py's web_unit_tests step, or land WSHL-08's folder discovery first: that step names two files today, so even schema-value.test.ts runs in no profile. Share one plural helper (or Intl.PluralRules) and one count and date formatter across the family. Name parsers and formatters for what they do (parseDays, formatGigabytes, integerFormat).
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06 asks for unit tests of pure and client behavior. Follow the repository's node:test precedent in apps/web/tests/unit rather than adding a runner, which would be a separate tooling decision. AGENTS.md: a test that no profile runs is not evidence.
findings.verifierNote: Helpers, the '1 hours ago.' plural and the format drift confirmed. Revised: verify.py:161-162 names its unit files, so schema-value.test.ts runs in no profile, and new tests need that list or WSHL-08's discovery.

findings.title: Operations lookup tables are keyed by string although the contract gives unions

locations.note: LABELS, ICONS and DOTS declared as Record<string, ...>
valueFor(name: string): a switch with a default; hold falls through
ICONS needs a fallback to Activity
LABELS has no fallback, so a missing entry renders an unnamed tile
valueFor runs twice per tile
exhaustive maps keyed by generated unions, the family's model
OperationCondition name and state are literal unions

findings.impact: When the contract gains a ninth check or renames a state and the client is regenerated, this still compiles, then renders a tile with no name or a default icon. At runtime parseLocalStatus already refuses unknown values. valueFor, at complexity 17, hides which checks have values.
